      "observations": [
        "Read the full fifteen-path 1591-line owned historical diff, including every changed browser test, EWS unit test, fake server, shared helper and Rust branch. Metadata and paths show Thunderbird/shared test infrastructure, with no Suite path or conditional body. The patch makes lastSentMessage protocol-neutral, adds explicit-identity SMTP/EWS account factories, EWS fixture options and TLS proxy support, and applies shared send, password, certificate and OAuth scenarios to both transports.",
        "The EWS fake now rejects absent Authorization and wrong recognized Basic or test_mail Bearer credentials with 401. The recognized Basic branch splits decoded credentials on a colon; other header prefixes fall through. This is a bounded test fixture, not complete HTTP authentication validation. Fake CreateItem records decoded MimeContent for the direct unique-subject oracle. Outgoing identity doFcc=false excludes filing a sent copy.",
        "Toolbar, menu and keyboard scenarios directly check unique subject text in lastSentMessage. Menu tasks are skipped on macOS. Three original EWS password tasks are explicitly skipped for Bug 1976128; the original ewsOutgoingServer declaration is not assigned, but these skipped tasks do not execute that path. The EWS bad-access-token prompt task is also skipped, including at the accepted revision, because the implementation uses a notification. Other OAuth tasks cover no tokens, no access token, expired access token and bad refresh token through the fake token server. Declared, skipped and directly asserted coverage stay separate.",
        "The bad-token setup changes the live cached OAuth object and invalidates the fake valid-token registry for incoming and outgoing tests. The helper now checks absent grantedScope before split, so an unknown nonempty token returns false. Reuse existing token-cache, fake-grant and unique-subject lessons rather than duplicate them. Current invalidateToken is named revokeToken. Current later OAuth assertions and Graph or telemetry extensions are not attributed to this patch.",
        "Certificate scenarios use four fixture certificate failures: wrong domain, expired, not yet valid and self-signed. Direct assertions inspect dialog hostname/text, matching certificate override and permanence, then retry and check sent payload. The retained 500 ms focus delay is an inherited test step, not a general waiting rule. Static inspection does not prove the native dialog or certificate transport ran.",
        "The original empty-password Basic branch returns an empty String while its comment says not to set Authorization. The same-revision client still passes that value to header(\"Authorization\", ...). No underlying HTTP header serialization was traced or run, so the empty string does not prove header omission. Current later code uses Option<String>, returns None for Basic/NTLM and adds the provider header only for Some; copied caller headers and Necko authentication remain distinct.",
        "Read relevant current account/window helpers, sequential fixture startup, fake authentication and payload handlers, token registry, direct-send assertion, bad-token setup/skip and current authentication producer/consumer. Added owned assertion messages are nonempty; a missing should alone is not a defect in another author's patch. Existing later helper assertions outside the owned change are not new patch defects. No Thunderbird test, lint, build, native dialog, real EWS/OAuth server, keyboard or accessibility run.",
        "Read complete retained Bug 1975707 description/comments 0–4, updates/footer. The initial issue says an authenticated request is not proof that the message was transmitted. The assigned browser tests add a unique-subject payload oracle, but the author explicitly leaves the umbrella open because unit tests and several mochitest scenarios remain. A later suggestion to extend EWS FCC/metadata coverage after Graph tests is future work, not an implemented EWS result. Dependencies are preserved as bounded locators; their unassigned bodies were not inferred.",
        "Read D256218 full creation-to-close timeline and all five actual inline bodies 1407145,1407146,1407156,1407161,1407167. The reviewer explicitly leaves argument/type documentation and common-setup reuse to author judgement. Every inline remains NotDone and there is no written response, but exact final source adds nsIMsgIdentity and SMTPServer|EWSServer parameter types to the toolbar/menu subtests. Source state, not the issue marker, establishes this adoption.",
        "The final patch shares createSMTPAccount/createEWSAccount and explicit-identity newComposeWindow helpers, while file setup still performs its own protocol-specific server/login/cleanup work. Certificate setup still creates accounts/identities directly. Thus optional code-sharing suggestions are neither a demanded full consolidation nor proof that all duplication was removed. Keep the local helper, subtest, task and transport naming families separate from any repository-wide rule. Parameter documentation names the actual argument roles; no unrelated JSDoc is rewritten.",
        "Direct payload assertions, TLS-dialog assertions and OAuth fake-state setup are already separated from the original skipped EWS password and bad-access-token prompt tasks in the source study. The original ewsOutgoingServer assignment gap is not executed by its skipped password tasks. The existing cache-poison, granted-scope and server-payload lessons remain linked. The empty Basic credential String still reaches the same-revision header caller; no wire-omission result is inferred from its comment. Current later optional-header behavior is separate. No send, FCC, auth prompt, certificate override, real provider, browser/unit test or accessibility execution occurred."
